The syntax error in the given Verilog module is the semicolon (`;`) placed after the `end` keyword of the last `else if` block. In Verilog, the `end` keyword is used to terminate a `begin` block and should not be followed by a semicolon when it is part of an `if-else` statement. This extra semicolon causes the compiler to misinterpret the subsequent code, leading to a syntax error and an "Invalid module instantiation" error.

To fix this, simply remove the semicolon after the `end` of the last `else if` block.

```verilog
module top_module (
	input clk,
	input a, 
	output reg [2:0] q
);

always @(posedge clk) begin
	if (a == 1) begin
		q <= 4;
	end else if (a == 0 && q == 6) begin
		q <= 0;
	end else if (a == 0 && q != 6) begin
		q <= q + 1;
	end
end

endmodule
```
